strategy.summary: createBookings() (src/bookings.ts) validates a booking's room, owner, UTC half-hour start and 30-minute-step length up to 4 hours, refuses clashes within a room, lists a room's bookings by start and lets only the owner cancel. Unit tests with Vitest against the real memoryStore() prove each rule, its boundaries and each refusal (BookingError with the reason).
inScope: book(): room, owner, start and length validation, with the BookingError message
book(): overlap rules within a room, across rooms and back-to-back
list(): order by start time, only the room's bookings
cancel(): by owner frees the time; by someone else or for an unknown id is refused
outOfScope: The app's database-backed BookingStore (not in this repository); tests use memoryStore() as the README says
assumptions: Room names match exactly (case-sensitive), as the code does: 'atlas' is refused.
An owner name is trimmed; a blank or whitespace-only owner is refused, as the code does.
A start given with a non-UTC offset is judged by its UTC instant (09:00+05:45 is 03:15Z, off the half hour).
The refusal messages in src/bookings.ts are the 'says why' of AC1; tests assert them exactly since they are the output under test.
Tests run against memoryStore() (the real in-memory store), with a fresh createBookings() per test; nothing is faked.
The at('HH:MM') date helper moves to test/support/time.ts and the existing test/bookings.test.ts imports it from there.
openQuestions: Should room names be matched case-insensitively ('atlas')? The code refuses them; tests follow the code.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the overlap boundaries (back-to-back bookings refused, or partial overlaps accepted)
risks.mitigation: TC7 covers each overlap shape; TC8 covers both back-to-back directions

risks.description: Length/start boundaries (30, 240, 270 minutes; seconds; non-UTC offsets) accepted or refused wrongly
risks.mitigation: TC4-TC6 test both sides of each boundary

risks.description: Someone other than the owner cancels a booking
risks.mitigation: TC12 checks the refusal and that the booking is still listed

acceptanceCriteria.text: A booking names one of Atlas, Borealis or Cosmos and its owner, starts on the hour or half hour UTC, and lasts 30 to 240 minutes in 30-minute steps; anything else is rejected with a BookingError saying why.
A booking overlapping another booking of the same room is rejected; different rooms never clash; a booking may start exactly when another ends.
A room's bookings are listed by start time.
Only the person who made a booking can cancel it, and cancelling frees its time.

testCases.title: books each of the office's rooms: %s
steps: it.each over ROOMS: book the room for ada at 09:00 for 60 minutes
testCases.expected: Returns the booking {id 1, room, owner 'ada', start 09:00, end 10:00}
testCases.rationale: Every named room must be bookable

testCases.title: refuses a room that is not one of the office's: $room
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'There is no room called "<room>".'
testCases.rationale: Unknown room refusal and its reason

testCases.title: refuses a booking whose owner is $label
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'A booking needs the name of the person making it.'

testCases.title: books $minutes minutes starting at $start
steps: Book Atlas at 09:30 for 30, 08:00 for 240, 10:00 for 90 minutes
testCases.expected: Each is booked with end = start + minutes
testCases.rationale: Accepted side of the start and length boundaries

testCases.title: refuses a start that is not on the hour or half hour UTC: $label
steps: Book Atlas starting 09:15Z, 09:00:30Z, 09:00+05:45, an invalid Date
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'A booking starts on the hour or the half hour.'
testCases.rationale: Refused side of the start rule, including UTC

testCases.title: refuses a booking lasting $minutes minutes
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'A booking lasts from 30 minutes to 4 hours, in steps of 30 minutes.'
testCases.rationale: Refused side of the length boundaries

testCases.title: refuses a booking of the same room that $shape
steps: grace books Atlas: same slot, starts inside it, ends inside it, contains it, lies within it
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'Atlas is already booked from 2026-03-02T10:00:00.000Z.'; list shows only ada's booking
testCases.rationale: Double bookings are the main risk

testCases.title: books a room back to back with another booking that $shape
steps: Book Atlas 11:00-11:30 (starts when it ends) / 09:30-10:00 (ends when it starts)

testCases.title: books the same time in a different room
lists a room's bookings by start time
testCases.expected: Atlas bookings in order 09:00, 11:30, 14:00, without the Cosmos one
testCases.rationale: Booking order differs from insertion order

testCases.title: cancelling a booking frees its time for another booking
testCases.expected: grace's booking succeeds and is the only one listed

testCases.title: refuses a cancellation by someone other than the person who made the booking
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'Only the person who made a booking can cancel it.'; booking still listed

testCases.title: refuses to cancel a booking that does not exist
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'There is no booking 42.'

review.standard: Working on the tests: Keep every assertion the accepted strategy describes (and list any dropped under deviations)
review.summary: TC8 (back-to-back) and TC9 (different room, line 113) check only book()'s return value and drop the strategy's list assertions ('list holds both' / 'Borealis list holds it'), so they never show that the new booking was kept alongside the existing one.
review.failureScenario: Suppose a regression in book()'s clash handling for touching bookings (or for a room's bookings across rooms) returns a booking without keeping both. For example, the existing 10:00-11:00 Atlas booking gets dropped, or the new booking is never stored. Both tests still pass because they only compare the returned object ({id: 2, ...}). The strategy's expected list check (`list('Atlas')` equal to [existing, new], or `list('Borealis')` equal to [booking]) would catch this. The tests also don't record the dropped assertion as a deviation.
